aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: WhatsApp’s green dot for online contacts reaches iPhone beta

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is making online status easier to spot on iPhone, but only for some beta testers right now.

According to WABetaInfo, the latest WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.26.10.72 adds a small green dot to show when a contact is active. The feature is rolling out through TestFlight and is not available to everyone yet.

The dot appears on a contact’s profile photo inside the chat info screen. You can reach that screen by tapping the contact’s name at the top of a conversation. For now, WhatsApp is not showing the dot in the main chat list or inside the conversation view.

The privacy rules still matter

The green dot does not make every contact easier to track. WABetaInfo says it follows WhatsApp’s existing last seen and online privacy settings, so it should not appear for people who hide their online status.

That detail matters because the indicator makes presence more visible at a glance. WhatsApp has been testing more convenience features lately, including a unified AI summary for unread messages, but online visibility is more sensitive than a shortcut for catching up on chats.

It also fits into WhatsApp’s wider privacy balancing act. Meta recently added Incognito Chat for WhatsApp and Meta AI, while this beta feature goes the other way: it makes a status that already exists easier to notice.

It is still a limited test

WABetaInfo says the green dot is available to some iOS beta testers and should reach more accounts over the coming weeks. A small number of App Store users may also see it as part of limited testing.

WhatsApp has not announced when the green dot will roll out to all iPhone users. Like most beta features, it could change before a wider release.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro Max may get a much bigger battery, leak claims

content.rendered:
Apple’s next Pro iPhones may bring a bigger battery story than expected, especially on the Pro Max model.

Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station says Chinese 3C certification information for Apple’s battery suppliers points to larger cells for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The smaller Pro model looks like a modest increase, while the Pro Max could get a much more noticeable jump.

The claimed numbers break down like this:

That would put the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max above 5,500mAh, up from the reported 5,088mAh battery in the U.S. iPhone 17 Pro Max. The China version would also move well past 5,000mAh, up from 4,823mAh.

The iPhone 18 Pro story is quieter. Its leaked capacity is only slightly higher than the iPhone 17 Pro, which means any real battery-life improvement would likely depend more on chip efficiency, modem changes, display tuning, and iOS behavior than on battery size alone.

The Pro Max number needs caution

Digital Chat Station did not present the Pro Max jump as a locked-in Apple spec. The post itself says the nearly 500mAh increase should be treated with doubt until verified.

That caveat matters. These devices are not announced, Apple has not confirmed the names or battery capacities, and certification listings can be hard to map cleanly to final retail models before launch.

Still, the numbers line up with the broader rumor pattern around Apple’s high-end iPhones. The iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to use the A20 Pro chip, and earlier reporting around standard iPhone 18 RAM already pointed to Apple keeping a clearer hardware gap between regular, Pro, and foldable models.

Why U.S. and China capacities differ

The leaked list gives different capacities for China and U.S. models. That is not new for Apple. Recent U.S. iPhones have leaned harder into eSIM-only designs, while models in some other regions continue to account for physical SIM hardware.

Removing the SIM tray can free up internal space, which is why the U.S. version of each leaked model has the larger listed capacity. It is a small difference on the iPhone 18 Pro, but it becomes more noticeable on the Pro Max.

In a follow-up Weibo post, Digital Chat Station said earlier supply-chain information had already pointed to the China iPhone 18 Pro Max entering the 5,000mAh range. The leaker also suggested that a 5,391mAh battery paired with the rumored 2nm A20 Pro chip could bring a clear battery-life improvement.

That is the part buyers would actually feel. A bigger battery is useful, but the larger question is whether Apple can turn the extra capacity and chip efficiency into longer real-world screen time without adding too much weight.

Apple’s fall lineup could be crowded

Apple is expected to introduce the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max this fall, possibly alongside its first foldable iPhone. The latest battery leak fits that wider premium push: Pro models with bigger batteries, a rumored foldable at the top end, and a more complicated iPhone Ultra and iPhone Air roadmap around them.

For now, the safe read is simple. The iPhone 18 Pro Max may be headed for a meaningful battery increase, while the regular Pro model looks more incremental. Until Apple announces the phones, treat the capacities as credible-looking leak data, not final specifications.

excerpt.rendered: A new leak points to larger iPhone 18 Pro batteries, with the Pro Max possibly crossing 5,500mAh in the U.S. model. Apple has not confirmed the specs.

title.rendered: GTA 6: Every weapon known to be in the game

content.rendered:
It’s been two-and-a-half years since GTA 6 got its announcement trailer. And, in that period, longtime fans and enthusiasts have thoroughly studied all its videos and screenshots out in the wild, extracting from them all different sorts of information. As a result, we currently have a rough idea about the weapons you’ll be able to see in the game come November 19.

The following list compiles all the glimpses of the weapons shown in official GTA 6 images and trailers, giving you a good idea of all that could be available at your disposal for wreaking havoc in Vice City and the state of Leonida. It also mentions where exactly these weapons can be spotted in the official GTA 6 media.

List of all GTA 6 weapons revealed so far

1. Hammer

In GTA 6’s first trailer, at the 0:58 mark, a woman can be seen with dual-wielded hammers. If this is something that the player does as well, it will be the first time a GTA game has provided the option to dual-wield melee weapons.

2. Baseball bat and shovel

The second image of the Port Gellhorn section on Rockstar’s website shows a man in the back resting a baseball bat on his shoulder. On the other hand, the man at the front can be seen grabbing the handle of what looks like a shovel. The latter weapon last featured in the series in 2004’s GTA San Andreas.

3. Golf club

On Rockstar’s website, in the Cal Hampton section, the first image depicts Cal holding a golf club. This seems like a natural addition to GTA 6’s arsenal given its main location, Vice City, was home to a prominent fictional golf course, known as the Leaf Links, in the city’s original rendition from 2002’s GTA Vice City.

4. Pool cue

In the second image of the Cal Hampton section, there is a pool cue each with Jason and Cal. While this may primarily be used to play the pool minigame, you can expect the game to let the player wield it as a weapon, similar to how things worked in past GTA titles such as GTA San Andreas.

5. Hawk & Little Morgan revolvers

Personalized versions of these revolvers appear in the Ultimate Edition screenshots on the official website. Apparently, these specific versions will be exclusively available for buyers of the pricier edition of GTA 6.

6. Mustang .357 revolver

In the third picture of the Ambrosia section, a woman can be seen brandishing a revolver with Mustang .357 engraved on it. Judging by the characters shown wielding this weapon, it seems fair to assume this may be frequently carried by a particular biker gang in the game.

7. Girardi ES9 and Klose K17 pistols

The personalized versions of these two pistols are also among the weapons shown in the Ultimate Edition screenshots for GTA 6. Similar to the aforementioned personalized revolvers, these are also exclusively available for buyers of the pricier edition.

8. Nipper .38 pistol

In the official GTA 6 cover art, Lucia is depicted holding a pistol with the text “Nipper .38” on it. A clearer version of this weapon can be found in the Media section, under “Artwork”, on Rockstar’s website. Additionally, this handgun also appears at the very end of the Only In Leonida section, under “Explore all”, where Lucia can be seen holstering it as Jason closes the car trunk.

9. Capo pistol

In the second image of the Raul Bautista section, you can see Raul Bautista in the driver’s seat holding a pistol with the Capo branding.

10. MP5-like SMG

In GTA 6 Trailer 2, at 1:15, we see a blink-and-you’ll-miss glimpse of Lucia and Jason equipped with an MP5-inspired submachine gun each.

11. M10-like SMG

Among the Vice City Vintage Pack items is an M10-inspired SMG, emblazoned with the iconic colors associated with GTA Vice City protagonist Tommy Vercetti. This weapon skin is a pre-order bonus and only available to those who buy the game before November 20, 2026.

12. Double-barreled shotgun

Moving on, the third image in the Grassrivers section on the official website depicts a man on a boat brandishing a double-barreled shotgun in the middle of an alligator-infested lake.

13. Guns inspired by Uzi, Remington 870, Benelli M4, AK47, and M249

In Trailer 2, at 2:10, there is a small segment about Phil’s Ammu-Nation, which offers a look at several different guns, including those inspired by the Uzi SMG, Remington 870 shotgun, Benelli M4 shotgun, AK47 rifle, and M249 light machine gun, the last of which is even shown being fired in the successive shot.

14. Duke carbine rifle

Among the batch of screenshots released in 2025, alongside Trailer 2, there was one that shows Jason aiming with a Duke-branded carbine rifle.

15. Duke assault sniper rifle and M14/M1A-like sniper rifle

In the first Grassrivers section image, a seated man can be seen with a Duke-branded assault sniper rifle, whereas another man standing right next to him has a different sniper rifle that looks like the game’s version of an M14 or an M1A.

16. Remington 700-like sniper rifle

Moreover, Mount Kalaga National Park section’s third picture depicts a couple of hunters walking towards a game they apparently shot down, with sniper rifles that look very similar to the Remington 700.

17. Grenade launcher

At the 1:58 mark, in GTA 6 Trailer 2, a female character, probably Lucia, blows up police vehicles using a grenade launcher. This is the only projectile weapon we have seen so far in the official clips and images. However, keeping in mind the franchise’s long association with rocket launchers, this may not be the only such weapon in the forthcoming game.

Rounding up

It’s important to note that the aforementioned list also contains those weapons that have only been shown as being used by GTA 6’s NPCs. Hence, there is no guarantee that the same will be available for Jason and Lucia to equip and use as well. If you’d like to learn more about the game’s cast, check out our list of GTA 6 characters.

On top of that, there are instances where things get changed in the time between the launch of a game’s trailer and its release date. This can easily result in items that were present in the promotional material not making it into the final version of the game. So, that is another thing to consider for those keen on GTA 6 and its lineup of weapons. While waiting for the game’s release, it’s also a great time to revisit some of the best GTA-like games to play and see how the genre has evolved over the years.

title.rendered: Everything new in iOS 27 beta 3

content.rendered:
Apple has released iOS 27 beta 3, introducing several new features and refinements ahead of the expected public release in September. The latest update adds more Siri customization options, a new Live Recognition accessibility feature, improvements to Photos and Shortcuts, updated AirPods controls, and a variety of interface tweaks throughout the system.

Here’s everything new in iOS 27 beta 3.

Siri voice customization

iOS 27 beta 3 finally enables Siri voice customization on supported devices. Although the option appeared in earlier beta releases, it wasn’t functional until now.

Users can now adjust Siri’s speaking speed and expressiveness, with two voice styles currently available in the beta.

Because the voice model runs entirely on-device, the feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone Air.

Live Recognition

Apple has added a new Live Recognition section within Settings > Accessibility. Powered by on-device Apple Intelligence, the feature uses the iPhone’s camera to identify and describe objects, scenes, and surroundings in real time.

Users can also:

  • Ask questions about what the camera sees
  • Set a default prompt
  • Create custom recognition activities

Reminders

The Reminders app receives a subtle visual refresh in beta 3. Apple has updated the app icon with a new Liquid Glass-inspired checklist bullet, bringing it more in line with the redesigned interface introduced in iOS 27.

Photo rating controls

The Photos section in Settings now includes a new Show Rating Controls toggle.

When enabled, star ratings appear while viewing photos and videos, and rating badges are also displayed on thumbnails, making it easier to organize and identify media.

Control Center

Control Center now displays additional cellular information even while connected to Wi-Fi.

Users can view:

  • Signal strength
  • Current network type (LTE or 5G)

This makes it easier to check cellular connectivity without disabling Wi-Fi.

Shortcuts

Apple has introduced a new preference for creating shortcuts. Users can now choose whether tapping the + button opens the Describe a Shortcut interface or takes them directly to the manual editor.

The change offers greater flexibility for both beginners and advanced Shortcuts users.

Wallpaper effect

iOS 27 beta 3 introduces a new animation for Notification Center.

When you swipe down, the wallpaper subject appears to extend above the Home Screen or the app currently in use, creating a subtle layered effect that complements Apple’s Liquid Glass design language.

AirPods adaptive controls

Adaptive Audio now includes a new slider that lets users fine-tune their listening experience.

Instead of relying solely on Apple’s automatic adjustments, users can now choose whether Adaptive mode favors:

  • More Transparency
  • Stronger Noise Cancellation

Home app

Apple has clarified the requirements for iOS 27 Apple Intelligence features in the Home app. According to the company, these features will require an iCloud+ 2TB subscription.

Maps

Apple has updated Maps with a new tooltip explaining that route preferences remain available. Users can access these options by tapping beneath the routing interface while requesting directions.

Lock Screen

Control Center buttons on the Lock Screen now display black icons instead of white ones when used with certain wallpapers, improving visibility and contrast.

5G+ support in India

iOS 27 beta 3 also enables 5G+ support in India for compatible carriers and supported iPhone models, giving users access to faster next-generation network capabilities where available.

While iOS 27 beta 3 doesn’t introduce major headline features, it delivers several meaningful refinements that improve day-to-day usability. From a more customizable Siri and smarter accessibility tools to better AirPods controls and thoughtful interface tweaks, Apple continues to polish the update ahead of its public release later this year.

Which iOS 27 beta 3 feature is your favorite? Let us know in the comments below.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: How to change your Roblox username and display name

content.rendered:
Roblox gives you two names, and they are not the same thing. Your display name is the name most players see first, and you can change it for free. Your username is your unique account name, and changing it requires Robux.

If you only want a fresh name in games and on your profile, change the display name first. Save the username change for when you really want to replace your account handle.

How to change your Roblox display name

Use this option if you want a new visible name without changing your login identity. Roblox may show this field as Display Name or just Name for some users.

  1. Log in to your Roblox account.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Select Account Info.
  4. Choose the Change Display Name pencil icon.
  5. Enter your new display name.
  6. Click Save.
  7. Refresh Roblox to check if the new name appears.

On the web, you can find Settings from the gear icon in the upper-right corner. On the Roblox mobile app, open the More menu with the three dots icon, then go to Settings.

You can change your display name only once every seven days. It must also follow Roblox rules, or Roblox may reset it back to your username.

How to change your Roblox username

Change your username only if you are fine spending Robux. Roblox does not treat this like a free profile edit, and even switching back to an old username requires Robux.

  1. Log in to your Roblox account.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Select Account Info.
  4. Click the Change Username pencil icon.
  5. Enter your new username.
  6. Enter your current Roblox password.
  7. Select Buy to confirm the change.

After the change, you can sign in with the new username and your current password. Before you hit Buy, check the Robux cost shown on the confirmation screen so you know exactly what you are paying.

What to know before changing either name

Your display name is more flexible, but it is not private or unique. Other players can use the same display name, and both your display name and username can appear across Roblox and its experiences.

Your username is stricter. You cannot take a username already used by another account, and you cannot swap usernames with an alt account. Roblox also says simple edits, such as only changing capitalization, do not get a discount.

One more important catch: past usernames can still be visible through Settings, your profile, and People search. If you are changing names because of account safety or suspicious activity, secure the account first and follow these Roblox hacking prevention tips before spending Robux on a new name.

Why the name change option is missing or not working

If Roblox will not save the new name, check these first:

  • You changed your display name recently: Wait until the seven-day limit ends.
  • The name is taken: Usernames must be unique, so try a different one.
  • The name breaks Roblox rules: Avoid personal info, impersonation, offensive words, and anything Roblox may filter.
  • You are in the wrong menu: Go to Settings > Account Info, not Avatar or Profile editing.
  • You do not have enough Robux: Username changes need Robux, so the purchase will not complete without enough balance.

For most players, changing the display name is the smarter first move. It is free, quick, and easy to undo after a week. Spend Robux on a username change only when the old handle itself is the problem.

If you are staying in Roblox mode, you can also check the latest Roblox game codes for free rewards across popular experiences.

You might also like:

  • What do Roblox icons and symbols mean?
  • How to appear offline in Roblox.
  • What it actually takes to get Verified on Roblox
  • How to customize your Roblox avatar

From iPhones and MacBooks to Android phones and AI tools, I’ve always enjoyed turning complicated features into simple, jargon-free guides. Recently, I switched sides and joined the Apple camp. Whether you want to try out new features, catch up on the latest news, or tweak your Apple devices, I’m here to help you get the most out of your tech.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio: With over 5 years of hands-on tech writing experience and more than 900 published articles, I’ve explored the best of Apple, Android, and Chrome OS. From iPhones and MacBooks to Pixel devices and Chromebooks, I break down complex features into simple, relatable guides—minus the jargon. Whether you’re customizing your iPhone, troubleshooting your Android, or tweaking Chrome OS settings, my goal is to help you get more out of your tech.

title.rendered: How to get MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins in Fortnite

content.rendered:
MCU-inspired Fortnite skins based on Iron Man and Captain America recently landed in the Item Shop. While the Iron Man skin looks to be modeled after the Mark III suit that appears in the armored hero’s film trilogy, the Captain America skin comes in two variants that take from the suits in Captain America: The First Avenger and Captain America: Civil War.

These MCU skins first appeared in Epic’s wildly popular online game in March 2026. They are now back for a limited time and are available to claim until July 6, 2026, by 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

The Captain America skins cost 2,000 V-Bucks each, while the Iron Man skin is available for 1,500 V-Bucks. Those looking to nab both can do so for a discount by purchasing the MCU Avengers bundle, which is priced at 2,800 V-Bucks. It includes the Iron Man skin and the Captain America skin inspired by his look in his inaugural solo film, alongside themed back bling and pickaxes.

Steps to claim MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins in Fortnite

  1. Launch Fortnite and select the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the Marvel promotion and select your preferred skin between Iron Man and Captain America, or select the MCU Avengers bundle if you want both.
  3. Lastly, press the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

Other MCU skins available in Fortnite

1. Captain America Sam Wilson

Price: 2,000 V-Bucks
Bonus items: Cap’s Shield back bling, Cap’s Shield pickaxe, and EXO-7 Falcon Wings glider.

2. Cap’s USO Shield (pickaxe and backbling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

3. Mark 1 Arc Reactor (backbling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks

4. Dum-E Arm (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

5. Missile Disposal (emote)

Price: 400 V-Bucks

6. BriteStar (skin)

Price: 2,000 V-Bucks
Bonus item: Brite’s Shield back bling and pickaxe

7. Brave and Brite (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Unlike the rest of the Marvel cosmetics available right now, BriteStar and Brave and Brite were originally created by Fortnite. In fact, BriteStar is a Captain America-like take by the devs on the game’s Brite Bomber character.

Wrapping up

Marvel has been a huge collaborator for Fortnite for a long time. The latter has not only added limited-time content over the years but also hosted full-fledged Marvel-themed events spanning an entire season. The latest MCU-inspired promotion is another chapter in the same long-running partnership between the two entertainment media giants.

Looking at the undying popularity of the two franchises, it is fair to expect their collaborative efforts to continue in the future. Especially with the Epic Games-Disney deal taking shape in the background, Marvel and Fortnite may join forces in bigger ways than before going ahead.

FAQs

Can you still get the MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins?

Yes, you can still get your hands on MCU Iron Man and Captain America until July 6, 2026, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

How much do the MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins cost?

These two skins cost a total of 2,800 V-Bucks when bought together in the MCU Avengers bundle.

What is included in the MCU Avengers bundle?

This bundle includes the Iron Man skin, Captain America skin, Mark 1 Reactor back bling, Dum-E Arm pickaxe, Cap’s USO Shield back bling and pickaxe, and Missile Disposal emote.

title.rendered: I turned my Galaxy S26 Ultra into a desktop. These DeX accessories made it possible

content.rendered:
I didn’t buy the Galaxy S26 Ultra expecting it to replace my laptop. However, after several weeks of using Samsung DeX every day, I stopped reaching for my laptop for most of my work. It handled my office work, browsing dozens of Chrome tabs, joining video calls, and even organizing photos — all from my S26 Ultra connected to a monitor.

That doesn’t mean everything is perfect. Some DeX-compatible accessories made the experience feel surprisingly close to Windows, while others turned into expensive desk clutter. If I were building a Samsung DeX desktop setup again today, I’d buy only the following S26 Ultra accessories and skip everything else.

What is Samsung DeX, and why does it matter?

The first time I heard about Samsung DeX, I assumed it was just screen mirroring with a fancy name. After actually using it, I realized it’s much more than that.

Samsung DeX (short for Desktop Experience) transforms compatible Galaxy phones into a desktop-style interface when connected to an external monitor or TV. Instead of seeing your phone’s home screen on a larger display like iPhone mirroring, you get a taskbar, resizable windows, keyboard shortcuts, and support for a mouse and keyboard.

Samsung also supports wireless DeX on compatible displays, though I found a wired connection to be more reliable for everyday work. For me, what makes DeX so useful is that I don’t need to carry both a phone and a laptop for light productivity. Simply plug the S26 Ultra into a monitor, pair a keyboard and mouse, and get a desktop-like workspace in seconds.

My complete Samsung DeX setup for the Galaxy S26 Ultra

Here’s exactly what’s on my desk, why each piece earned its spot, and what I’d skip if I built this again.

1. Belkin 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station: It improved the whole experience

I underestimated how much a phone stand would matter until I spent an entire afternoon with my S26 Ultra lying flat on the desk. The Belkin 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station made my entire workspace cable-free and more organized. It lets you keep your phone, Galaxy Buds, and smartwatch in one dedicated spot.

During long DeX sessions, I’d often pick up my phone to respond to a message and simply snap it back onto the charger, thanks to the strong magnetic connection with my Qi2 magnetic case. Another good feature is its adjustable design. You can keep the phone upright in portrait mode for notifications or rotate it to landscape when watching videos during breaks.

The included 45W power adapter meant I didn’t have to buy another charger, and the charging station supports Qi2.2 25W wireless charging. That said, this isn’t an essential Samsung DeX accessory. It doesn’t improve DeX performance or add new functionality like a USB-C hub or monitor does.

Pros

  • Charges your phone, earbuds, and smartwatch from one station
  • Compact, foldable design keeps the desk clutter-free
  • Adjustable viewing angles let you use the phone while charging
  • Strong magnetic alignment makes docking the phone effortless

Cons

  • Doesn’t directly improve DeX performance
  • Wireless charging can generate extra heat
  • Premium price compared to basic wireless chargers

Best for: Anyone planning to use DeX for more than an hour at a time.

Check out on Amazon

2. UGREEN Revodok Pro 109 USB-C Hub: The real hero of my S26 Ultra DeX setup

If one accessory made DeX possible, it was the USB-C hub. I initially tried connecting the phone with a basic USB-C cable and quickly realized it wasn’t enough. Technically, Samsung DeX does support a simple USB-C-to-HDMI connection, but this setup doesn’t let you connect multiple peripherals at the same time.

Samsung recommends using compatible HDMI adapters or USB-C hubs with Power Delivery for the best DeX experience, and the UGREEN Revodok Pro checks all the boxes. It offers 9 ports, including a 10 Gbps USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 port, two 10 Gbps USB-A ports, 4K@60Hz HDMI, 100W Power Delivery, an RJ45 port, and an SD/microSD card reader.

I used the HDMI to connect a monitor, the USB ports for my keyboard, mouse, and SSD, and plugged a 45W charger into the Power Delivery port so the phone didn’t slowly drain throughout extended use. Overall, this single accessory turned my S26 Ultra into a workstation.

Pros

  • Turns a Galaxy phone into a complete desktop workstation
  • Compact aluminum build that’s easy to carry
  • Plug-and-play with Samsung DeX, no drivers required

Cons

  • Gets warm under heavy use
  • Requires a compatible USB-C charger for pass-through charging

Best For: If you are serious about building a reliable Samsung DeX workstation.

Check out on Amazon

3. MNN 15.6inch Portable Monitor: The upgrade that changed everything

Samsung no longer supports DeX for PC on devices running One UI 7 or later, including the Galaxy S26 series. That means you can’t simply plug your phone into a Windows PC and launch DeX inside a desktop window like you could on older Galaxy phones.

If you want the full Samsung DeX desktop experience, you now need to connect your Galaxy S26 Ultra directly to an external monitor or TV. That’s exactly why the MNN 15.6-inch Portable Monitor became one of my must-have desk accessories. The 15.6-inch Full HD IPS display is the sweet spot for productivity.

It’s large enough to multitask comfortably, yet compact enough to carry around in a backpack. I could keep Google Docs open beside Chrome, Gmail, and YouTube without constantly switching apps. The monitor also comes with two USB-C ports, and the built-in smart cover doubles as a stand, which helped me work anywhere.

Pros

  • 15.6-inch display provides more workspace than the phone screen
  • Lightweight and easy to travel with
  • Matte display helps reduce reflections
  • Smart cover works as a built-in stand

Cons

  • Built-in speakers are only average
  • Limited to a 60Hz refresh rate
  • You’ll still need a compatible USB-C hub or HDMI adapter for most DeX setups

Best for: Students, writers, and remote workers who travel frequently.

Check out on Amazon

4. ProtoArc XK01 Bluetooth Keyboard: It made writing feel natural

Typing thousands of words on a phone screen gets old very quickly. The ProtoArc Bluetooth keyboard instantly made DeX work like a Windows laptop. It let me use familiar keyboard shortcuts and navigate windows more efficiently. With the Galaxy S26 Ultra, which no longer supports DeX for PC, it becomes even more important.

The best part is that it combines portability with a full-size typing experience. Unlike compact travel keyboards that feel cramped, you get full-sized keys and even a numeric pad, which makes typing more comfortable. Since it connects over Bluetooth, I didn’t have to occupy one of the USB ports on my hub.

It isn’t a mechanical keyboard, so don’t expect tactile feedback. But for productivity, I actually preferred its quieter keys while writing at cafes or libraries.

Pros

  • Full-size layout with number pad makes long typing sessions comfortable
  • Foldable design is easy to carry
  • Reliable connection with the Galaxy S26 Ultra
  • Supports keyboard shortcuts for a more desktop-like workflow

Cons

  • Slight learning curve for Android shortcuts
  • Not the most compact travel keyboard
  • Premium price compared to basic Bluetooth keyboards

Best for: Anyone who spends hours writing, replying to emails, or working in documents.

Check out on Amazon

5. Logitech Pebble Mouse 2: Work on your DeX like Windows

Before adding a wireless mouse to my Samsung DeX setup, I was relying on my Galaxy S26 Ultra’s touchscreen to act as the touchpad, but it never really felt right. The moment I paired the Logitech Pebble Mouse 2, DeX started feeling like an actual desktop operating system.

Once the mouse is connected, you get precise cursor control, right-click context menus, drag-and-drop support, text selection, and much smoother window management. All of this made DeX far more productive and faster to use than relying on touch controls alone.

Logitech built the mouse slim and lightweight, so it didn’t take up much room in my backpack. One feature I appreciated was its Bluetooth connectivity. The connection remained stable throughout long work sessions, and I never noticed any lag while navigating DeX. However, it’s not designed for gaming or professional design work.

Pros

  • Smooth and accurate cursor tracking
  • Bluetooth connection keeps USB ports free
  • Quiet clicks are ideal for shared workspaces
  • Excellent battery life with minimal maintenance

Cons

  • Not intended for gaming or high-DPI creative work
  • Compact size may feel small for users with larger hands
  • Limited customization

Best for: If you are planning to use DeX as your primary desktop environment.

Check out on Amazon

6. Samsung Portable SSD T9: The accessory that eliminated my storage anxiety

Once I started using my Galaxy S26 Ultra as my main work device, storage filled up much faster than I expected. Screenshots, downloaded files, videos, and project folders quickly ate into my phone’s internal storage.

That’s where the Samsung Portable SSD T9 came to the rescue. Attached through my USB-C hub, the SSD was instantly recognized by Samsung DeX’s My Files, just like any external drive. Being able to transfer files, save backups, and access large media libraries without relying on cloud storage became incredibly convenient.

The T9 also offers up to 2,000 MB/s read and write speeds, making large file transfers quick and hassle-free. Its compact, durable design was easy to toss into my backpack, so I always had extra storage wherever I worked.

Pros

  • Extremely fast transfers
  • Instantly recognized by Samsung DeX
  • Compact, rugged design that’s easy to carry
  • Supports hardware encryption for added security

Cons

  • More expensive than a USB flash drive
  • Requires a USB-C hub in most wired DeX setups

Best for: Creators, photographers, and anyone working with large files.

Check out on Amazon

Samsung DeX accessories that weren’t worth buying

Not every accessory made my DeX setup better. In fact, a few purchases ended up collecting dust.

A major letdown is that USB-C hubs without HDMI don’t support Samsung DeX. Samsung suggests using a suitable USB-C-to-HDMI adapter or a USB-C hub with video support; otherwise, DeX simply won’t launch on an external display.

I also skipped buying a Samsung DeX Station or DeX Pad. While these older accessories were designed for previous Galaxy devices, they’re unnecessary for the Galaxy S26 Ultra. A compatible USB-C hub and monitor can replace them and deliver the same desktop-like experience.

Lastly, I tried using wireless DeX on a TV. It worked fine for light browsing and similar tasks, but there were noticeable lag and compression issues when dragging windows around or typing. I’d recommend sticking with a wired connection instead.

Sometimes the simplest setup really is the best one.

How Samsung DeX performed for my daily work tasks

This is where DeX genuinely surprised me.

Writing articles felt almost identical to working on a Windows laptop. Chrome handled multiple tabs better than I expected, although opening dozens at once eventually slowed things down.

Google Docs, Microsoft Word, Gmail, Slack, and Notion all worked reliably enough that I didn’t need to touch my phone. Streaming YouTube while working also caused no issues, and photo organization was straightforward.

Where DeX struggled was heavier creative work. Video editing remained slower than I’d like, and certain desktop software simply doesn’t exist on Android.

What I wish I knew before building my Samsung DeX setup

  • Not every USB-C hub supports video output. I ended up wasting time figuring out why the setup wasn’t working.
  • Power delivery matters more than you think. DeX drains battery faster than normal phone use, especially with external displays connected.
  • Don’t overspend on accessories. Expensive doesn’t automatically mean better.
  • Invest in a keyboard and mouse. DeX becomes far more productive once you stop relying on the phone’s touchscreen.
  • Finally, DeX isn’t trying to replace Windows. Once I stopped expecting a desktop operating system and started treating it as a highly optimized Android desktop, the experience became much more enjoyable.

Is Samsung DeX good enough to replace a laptop?

For me, yes! But only for the right kind of work.

If your day revolves around writing, research, web apps, email, presentations, and meetings, DeX is shockingly capable. However, for editing 4K videos, compiling software, running virtual machines, or using specialized desktop applications, you’ll still want a traditional laptop.

The biggest surprise wasn’t that Samsung DeX could replace my laptop. It was realizing how often I didn’t actually need a laptop in the first place.

Final verdict: Is the Samsung DeX setup worth it?

Before trying Samsung DeX, I assumed it was a feature I’d show friends once and forget. Instead, it became part of my daily workflow.

If I had to rebuild this setup from scratch, I’d buy the USB-C hub first, followed by a monitor, Bluetooth keyboard, wireless mouse, phone stand, and finally an external SSD. These accessories transformed the Galaxy S26 Ultra from an excellent smartphone into a surprisingly capable workstation.

Have you tried Samsung DeX yet? Share your experience in the comments below!

Having honed her writing and editing skills over 5 years at renowned media houses like TechBurner, Ava crafts informative and engaging articles including troubleshooting guides, product reviews, editorials at iGeeksBlog. When not typing, you can find her exploring the latest Apple releases or pondering the future of tech innovation."

About Ava Biswas

  • Ava is a die-hard Apple aficionado and loves testing the latest tech gadgets.
  • She is always on the lookout for issues Apple users are facing, finds solutions, and crafts troubleshooting guides.
  • Her goal to make tech easy for everyone encouraged her to break down complex concepts into easily digestible content.

Experience

Ava has been employing her professional writing and editing skills for over 4 years at renowned media houses like TechBurner and iGeeksBlog. Using her expertise, she crafts informative and engaging How-To's, troubleshooting guides, product reviews, and editorials. When not typing, you can find her exploring the latest Apple releases or pondering new tech innovations.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Pro Max joins America’s 250-year time capsule

content.rendered:
An orange iPhone 17 Pro Max is heading into America’s Time Capsule, giving Apple’s current flagship a strange kind of immortality: it is meant to be seen again in 2276.

The device appears on America250’s official time capsule contents page. The capsule is part of the United States’ 250th anniversary celebration and is scheduled to be buried in Philadelphia on July 4, 2026.

That makes the iPhone less of a gadget story and more of a cultural snapshot. The phone is being placed next to letters, state artifacts, federal contributions, sports memorabilia, and other objects meant to show future Americans what the country looked like in 2026.

Why this iPhone makes sense

The iPhone 17 Pro Max is not just a popular phone; it is a pocket-sized record of how people communicate, shoot photos, use apps, and carry most of their digital lives in one object.

The orange finish also matters. Apple’s Cosmic Orange color turned the Pro model into something more visually memorable than the usual dark or silver flagship, and the color has already spilled into the broader Cosmic Orange iPhone trend.

The time capsule choice also lands after the iPhone 17 Pro Max had another unusual public moment. Earlier this year, NASA astronauts used an iPhone 17 Pro Max to capture Earth during Artemis II, turning the same model into a space-story device before it became a time-capsule object.

What else is inside the capsule

Axios reported that the 900-pound steel capsule includes more than 200 letters and artifacts from the federal government, all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and five territories. Other reported items include a whale bone from Maine, a diamond from Arkansas, a George Washington prayer medal from Utah, and a coin featuring Steve Jobs from California.

Ohio’s contribution includes a piece of fabric from the Wright Flyer, tying the capsule back to one of the country’s defining aviation moments. That contrast is the fun part: future Americans may find early-flight history and an orange iPhone in the same national memory box.

The capsule is expected to stay sealed for 250 years and be opened on America’s 500th birthday in 2276. By then, the iPhone 17 Pro Max will probably look ancient. But that is exactly why it belongs there.

excerpt.rendered: America’s Time Capsule will include an orange iPhone 17 Pro Max, preserving Apple’s 2026 flagship as a cultural artifact for 2276.

title.rendered: Foldable iPhone Ultra could follow iPhone X launch strategy, Kuo says

content.rendered:
Apple could introduce its first foldable iPhone alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in September, but the device may not be available to order immediately.

Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Apple is likely to “repeat the iPhone X story” with the foldable iPhone, which is rumored to launch as the iPhone Ultra. The device could be announced with the rest of the lineup before pre-orders begin several weeks later.

Delayed pre-orders due to production challenges

Kuo says early production of the foldable iPhone has been limited by manufacturing challenges, which could push availability later than the standard iPhone 18 Pro models.

Apple followed a similar strategy with the iPhone X in 2017. The company announced the iPhone X alongside the iPhone 8 and iPhone 8 Plus on September 12, but while iPhone 8 pre-orders started three days later, customers had to wait until October 27 to order the iPhone X.

A similar timeline could happen again in 2026, with the foldable iPhone Ultra potentially becoming available for pre-order in the fourth quarter.

iPhone Ultra could sell out quickly

Kuo estimates that Apple’s first foldable iPhone could start at between $2,299 and $2,499 in the U.S., making it one of the most expensive iPhone models ever released.

Kuo believes the foldable iPhone Ultra could sell out immediately after pre-orders open, with delivery times quickly stretching to four to six weeks or longer due to limited early supply.

The analyst also says Apple’s suppliers are expected to ship around 7 to 8 million foldable iPhone units in 2026. In comparison, combined shipments for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are expected to reach around 20 to 22 million units.

If Kuo’s prediction is accurate, Apple could reveal the foldable iPhone Ultra in September alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, but customers may need to wait until October or later before they can order one.

Would you wait longer for the foldable iPhone Ultra or choose the iPhone 18 Pro instead? Let us know in the comments below.

excerpt.rendered: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo believes Apple could launch the foldable iPhone Ultra using the same strategy it used for the iPhone X, with a September announcement followed by delayed pre-orders.

title.rendered: I asked Gemini to find Android apps instead of searching the Play Store: It actually worked

content.rendered:
Every time I need an Android app, my instinct tells me to open the Play Store and begin my search there. Then scroll through dozens of apps, check their reviews, and look for recommendations online. This process works just fine, but it’s rather inefficient. The problem is that the Play Store expects me to know exactly what I’m looking for.

Google’s new Gemini integration with Google Play aims to change that. Instead of searching with keywords, you simply describe what you need in natural language, and Gemini recommends apps while pulling listings directly from Google Play. Here’s how I used Gemini to find Android apps.

Google quietly changed how you can discover Android apps

Google recently previewed a new Google Play Connected App inside Gemini at I/O 2026. Once enabled, Gemini can access relevant Google Play information such as search results, app library details, and purchase eligibility to recommend the perfect apps.

At first glance, it sounds like a small addition. In reality, it changes one of Android’s oldest habits: searching for apps. Normally, searching the Play Store means reducing your needs into a few keywords. The Play Store then returns hundreds of results based largely on keywords, popularity, ratings, downloads, and sponsored ads.

Gemini approaches the same problem differently. Instead of searching keywords, you describe what you actually want. For example, I asked Gemini that I need a free PDF editor that works offline. It understands the request, explains its recommendations, and displays Google Play listings. Tapping the app card sends you directly to the installation page.

It feels less like using a search engine and more like asking someone who already knows the Play Store inside out.

How I used Gemini to search apps on Play Store

The first thing I had to do was enable the feature. I have tested it with my Gemini Pro account. It’s still rolling out on other Gemini slabs.

  1. Open the Gemini app on your Android device.
  2. Go to the sidebar and tap the gear icon at the top to open Settings.
  3. Select Personal Intelligence >Connected Apps.
  4. Scroll down the Google services list and toggle on Google Play.
  5. After enabling it, Gemini will ask for permission to access Google Play. Tap Connect to continue. Note that Gemini may share parts of your conversation with Google Play to fulfill requests.

Once connected, I decided to skip opening the Play Store altogether. Instead, I asked Gemini: Can you recommend the best app to read the latest manga? Within seconds, Gemini responded with something I wasn’t expecting.

Instead of simply listing manga app names, it explained why each recommendation deserved consideration. It recommended MANGA Plus by Shueisha, Shonen Jump Manga & Comics, and WEBTOON. For each app, Gemini gave a short explanation. For example, it highlighted that MANGA Plus offers official simultaneous chapter releases directly from Japan.

Below those appeared actual Google Play cards. Each card showed:

  • App icon
  • Rating
  • Download count
  • Developer
  • Quick shortcut

As soon as I tapped Shonen Jump Manga & Comics, Gemini took me to its listing on the Google Play Store, where I could install it normally. Moreover, you can ask Gemini to search for and purchase in-app digital items, subscriptions, or digital gift cards for supported stores and apps on your device.

Where Gemini was surprisingly better

After using it, I realized Gemini isn’t trying to improve Play Store search. It’s trying to replace the part of app discovery that has always been frustrating.

It understands intent instead of keywords

This is easily the biggest improvement. When I searched for a manga app, I wasn’t thinking about keywords. I simply described what I wanted. That’s a completely different experience.

Traditional search expects users to know which keywords developers have optimized for. Gemini doesn’t. It understands the request itself. That’s a huge advantage for anyone who isn’t sure what they’re looking for.

Gemini explains recommendations

One thing I immediately appreciated was that Gemini didn’t just throw links at me. It explained why it picked each app. Thanks to Personal Intelligence, the AI knows me very well and gives the summaries accordingly.

Those explanations save time. More importantly, they help you make better decisions. I didn’t need to open multiple Play Store pages and compare features manually.

Discovery feels smarter

Play Store search often rewards popularity. Gemini seems to reward relevance. That’s an important distinction.

If I ask for an app for reading manga legally, I don’t necessarily want the app with the highest download count. I want the one that best fits my needs. Gemini seems much better at understanding that difference.

Less scrolling

Perhaps my favorite part? I spent almost no time scrolling.

Normally, finding a good app means opening multiple listings, checking ratings, reading descriptions, and comparing screenshots. Gemini condensed much of that work into a single conversation.

Where the Play Store still wins

As impressive as Gemini is, I don’t think it replaces the Play Store. At least not yet.

Exact searches are still faster

If I already know the app I want, I’ll continue using Play Store search.

Searching for WhatsApp, Spotify, Instagram, or Adobe Lightroom is still quicker than opening Gemini first.

Browsing is better inside the Play Store

Sometimes I don’t want recommendations; instead, I just want to browse. The Play Store still has advantages here.

Features like:

  • Top Charts
  • Editor’s Choice
  • New Releases
  • Trending Games

don’t really have an equivalent inside Gemini. Those sections are still useful when you’re casually exploring.

AI can still be too general

Although my first experience was positive, AI recommendations can sometimes lean toward obvious or mainstream suggestions.

That isn’t necessarily bad. But users looking for very niche or highly specialized apps may still end up refining their prompts or browsing manually.

Tips that made Gemini give better recommendations

One thing I noticed almost immediately is that better prompts produce better recommendations. Instead of typing short searches, treat Gemini like you’re asking another person.

Rather than saying Note app, try: Recommend a note-taking app with Markdown support that syncs between Android and Windows.

Instead of budget app, try: I need a budgeting app for couples that works offline and doesn’t require a subscription.

The more context you provide, the better Gemini understands what you’re actually trying to accomplish.

Here are a few prompt ideas I’d recommend trying:

  • Recommend an offline music player without ads.
  • Find a lightweight photo editor for low-end Android phones.
  • Suggest the best automatic habit tracker with widgets for beginners.

These kinds of prompts showcase why conversational search is more powerful than keyword search.

What this means for the future of the Play Store

I don’t think Google built this feature because Play Store search is broken. It built it because search itself is changing. For decades, software discovery has relied on keywords.

Users adapted to machines. Now machines are adapting to users. That’s a much bigger shift than simply adding AI to the Google Play Store.

If Google continues improving Gemini’s recommendations, I can imagine a future where most people never type keywords into the Play Store again. Instead, they’ll ask questions. Developers may also need to rethink how they optimize their apps.

Today, visibility is highly dependent on titles, keywords, downloads, and reviews. Tomorrow, AI could place greater emphasis on whether an app actually satisfies a user’s request. That’s a fundamental change in app discovery.

Should you start using Gemini instead of the Play Store?

After trying it myself, I don’t think the answer is choosing one over the other. The better approach is using both.

Use Gemini when you:

  • Don’t know which app to install.
  • Want recommendations based on your needs.
  • Want explanations before downloading.
  • Are looking for alternatives.

Use the Play Store when you:

  • Already know the app’s name.
  • Are browsing trending apps.
  • Want to explore categories manually.

For me, Gemini has become the starting point. The Play Store has become the destination. That’s a surprisingly natural workflow.

Final thoughts

I expected Gemini’s Google Play integration to be another AI feature I’d try once and forget about. Instead, it solved a problem I’ve had with the Play Store for years.

Searching for apps has always required guessing the right keywords and digging through pages of results. Gemini removes much of that guesswork by letting me describe what I actually want, then explaining why certain apps fit my needs before sending me to the Play Store to install them.

That said, I don’t see Gemini replacing the Play Store anytime soon. The Play Store is still the fastest way to download apps you already know, browse top charts, or explore new releases. But when it comes to discovering the right app for a specific task, Gemini already feels like the smarter place to start.

Which one will you choose: Gemini or the traditional Play Store for app recommendations? Share your opinion in the comments below!

title.rendered: iPhone Fold could push foldable phone prices higher in 2026

content.rendered:
Apple has not announced a foldable iPhone yet, but its expected entry into the category is already showing up in analyst forecasts.

Counterpoint Research expects the average selling price of foldable smartphones to rise 18% year over year in 2026. The main reason is the market’s shift toward book-style foldables, the same form factor Apple is widely expected to use for its first foldable iPhone.

Book-style foldables are pulling prices up

Counterpoint says the two main foldable designs are moving in opposite directions. Clamshell foldables are getting cheaper as more brands enter the market and production scales up. Book-style foldables, however, remain more expensive because they tend to use larger displays, better hinges, bigger batteries, stronger cameras, and more productivity-focused features.

That matters because book-style models are now taking a larger share of total foldable shipments. So even if cheaper flip-style foldables continue to exist, the overall foldable market can still become pricier when more buyers move toward the larger, tablet-like designs.

Counterpoint’s price-band data makes that shift clearer. In 2025, more than half of foldable smartphones were priced below $1,200 on a wholesale basis, while about one in three foldables sat above $1,600. In 2026, models above $1,600 are expected to account for 60% of shipments, while models under $1,200 are expected to fall below 30%.

Apple could make the high end feel normal

Counterpoint says Apple’s entry is expected to support the upward pricing trend by keeping attention on high-priced foldables. The firm also expects Apple to increase interest in software continuity, app support, and productivity across the category.

That is the key part for Apple. A foldable iPhone cannot be expensive only because it folds. It has to make the larger screen feel useful for everyday work: reading, browsing, messaging, video, multitasking, and moving between apps without losing context.

The rumor cycle already points to Apple treating the foldable as a new premium lane rather than a one-off experiment. Recent reports around the iPhone Ultra and iPhone Air roadmap suggest the foldable model could sit above the regular Pro line, with Apple using “Ultra” branding to separate it from standard iPhones.

For buyers, the takeaway is simple. Apple’s first foldable may not make foldable phones cheaper. If Counterpoint’s forecast is right, it could do the opposite at first: make the top end of the foldable market look more normal, while cheaper clamshell models keep fighting for the lower premium tier.

excerpt.rendered: Counterpoint expects foldable phone prices to rise in 2026 as book-style models grow. Apple’s rumored iPhone Fold could help normalize the premium tier.

title.rendered: iCloud+ users are getting two new Apple Intelligence perks with iOS 27

content.rendered:
Apple is adding two new benefits for iCloud+ subscribers with iOS 27, giving users access to higher limits for some Apple Intelligence features and new AI-powered tools for HomeKit Secure Video cameras.

The new perks come at no additional cost for eligible iCloud+ subscribers, though Apple has not shared the exact requirements for every storage tier.

Higher Apple Intelligence usage limits

Apple says some new and enhanced Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27 will have daily usage limits because they depend on powerful server models that are more expensive to operate.

However, users subscribed to “most” iCloud+ storage plans will receive increased access to these features. This likely means higher usage limits than users on the free 5GB iCloud plan receive, though the entry-level 50GB iCloud+ tier may not include the same benefits.

One of the biggest examples is the revamped Image Playground app. Starting with iOS 27, Image Playground can generate photorealistic images thanks to improved Apple Intelligence models. The company has not revealed the exact daily generation limits or how much extra access iCloud+ users will receive.

The improvements come as Apple Intelligence gains access to upgraded models powered by Google’s Gemini technology, bringing more capable AI features across supported devices.

New HomeKit Secure Video features

iOS 27 also adds new Apple Intelligence capabilities for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras in the Home app.

The new features include generated video descriptions, search support for camera clips, and automatic highlights of important moments from recorded footage.

These camera upgrades are expected to require at least the 200GB iCloud+ plan, priced at $2.99 per month. Users with Apple One Family and Apple One Premier subscriptions should also get access, as both include larger iCloud storage plans.

The new benefits will arrive alongside iOS 27 as Apple continues adding more features to its paid iCloud+ subscription plans.

Do these new Apple Intelligence features make iCloud+ worth paying for? Let us know in the comments below.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Volkswagen preparing Apple Wallet car key support, code suggests

content.rendered:
Volkswagen is preparing to add Apple Wallet car key support to future vehicles, according to references found in new Apple server-side code.

The code suggests that Volkswagen is working on adopting Apple’s digital car key feature, though it does not reveal which vehicle models will support it or when the feature will become available.

How Apple Wallet car keys work

Apple Wallet car keys allow users to store a digital version of their vehicle key on an iPhone or Apple Watch. Once set up, the feature can be used to lock, unlock, and start a compatible vehicle without using a physical key.

Depending on the vehicle and supported technology, users can access their car by holding their device near the door handle or by keeping their iPhone or Apple Watch nearby.

Apple Wallet car keys can also be shared with other users, making it possible to provide temporary or permanent access without handing over a physical key.

The discovery indicates that Volkswagen could soon join the list of automakers that allow drivers to replace a traditional car key with their iPhone or Apple Watch.

More automakers continue adding support

Volkswagen has not officially announced Apple Wallet car key integration yet, so details such as supported models, regions, and launch timing remain unknown.

If the feature rolls out, Volkswagen will join several automakers that already support Apple’s car key system, including Audi, BMW, Hyundai, Kia, Genesis, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, and others.

Apple Wallet car keys are already available from several automakers, including Audi, BMW, Hyundai, Kia, Genesis, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, and others. Volkswagen would be another major addition to the list once support becomes available.

More details should become available once Volkswagen or Apple officially confirms the feature rollout.

Would you replace your physical car key with your iPhone or Apple Watch? Let us know in the comments below.

title.rendered: I started using Snapchat’s Arrival Notifications instead of texting “I’m here”

content.rendered:
My family has a simple rule whenever I’m traveling: send a message after I reach. I rarely ignore it, but I do forget it. By the time I’ve parked the car, checked into a hotel, or started unpacking, that quick “Reached” text is already out of my head. Since I already use Snapchat with the same people, I switched to Arrival Notifications. The feature turned out to be a much easier way to handle those routine check-ins because the app sends them automatically when I arrive. It’s also a good reminder that Snapchat has added plenty of useful features beyond Snapchat Plus, many of which are available to everyone.

Continue reading to learn everything you need to know about Arrival Notifications on Snapchat.

What are Snapchat Arrival Notifications?

Arrival Notifications are a Snap Map feature that automatically lets selected friends know when you’ve reached a destination. You can save places like your home, office, college, a hotel, or any other location, then choose who should receive the notification.

When you arrive, Snapchat sends your friend a push notification along with a message in your chat. They don’t need to ask whether you’ve reached because the app has already answered the question.

I still send messages when I actually want to start a conversation. Arrival Notifications only replace the repetitive “Reached safely” update that rarely needs anything more.

Why I stopped texting “Reached”

Reaching somewhere is usually the busiest part of the trip. Between parking, finding the entrance, collecting luggage, or checking into a hotel, opening Snapchat isn’t the first thing on my mind. Arrival Notifications quietly handle the check-in while I’m doing everything else.

How to enable and use Snapchat Arrival Notifications

Snapchat lets you set them up from either a friend’s profile or an existing chat.

From a friend’s profile

  1. Open your friend’s profile and scroll to the Snap Map section.
  2. Tap the Add button to add a new location.
  3. Here, select Arrival Notifications.
  4. Next, search the destination you want to save, then tap Set Location.
  5. Now, under Arrival Notifications, turn on the toggle next to the location you want.
  6. Choose One Time or Every Time, and you are done.

From a chat

  1. Open your conversation with the friend.
  2. Tap the Map icon.
  3. Tap Add under Arrival Notifications.
  4. Select your destination.
  5. Enable the toggle.
  6. Choose One Time or Every Time.

One detail is easy to miss. Saving a location doesn’t activate notifications automatically. You’ll still need to switch the toggle on before the feature starts working.

Note: The option to set up Arrival Notifications from a chat wasn’t available on my account, so I couldn’t verify it. The steps above are based on Snapchat’s official support documentation.

One Time or Every Time? Don’t use the same option everywhere

One Time is the option I end up using most. It works well for hotels, Airbnb stays, a friend’s house, or anywhere I’m only visiting once. The notification expires after 24 hours, so there’s nothing to clean up later.

I reserve Every Time for places I visit regularly. Home has stayed on since the day I set it up because that’s where my family usually expects an arrival update. For everything else, it depends on how often I visit. A hotel or a friend’s house stays on One Time, while places I visit every week are the only ones that ever get the permanent option.

After a couple of trips, I also realized there’s no point in keeping Every Time enabled for locations I’ll probably never visit again. It only adds clutter the next time I open the list.

Three privacy habits I recommend

Arrival Notifications rely on location sharing, so I spent a few minutes tweaking a couple of settings before making them part of my routine. These are the habits I’ve stuck with ever since.

  • Share with people who actually need updates: I treat Arrival Notifications as a feature for people who genuinely expect an arrival update. Family members, a partner, or a close friend usually make sense. Everyone else doesn’t need automatic notifications every time I reach somewhere.
  • Delete temporary locations: Temporary places never stay in my saved list for long. Once a trip is over, I remove hotels and vacation rentals instead of leaving them there indefinitely. It keeps the list organized and avoids unnecessary location reminders.
  • Review your Snap Map sharing settings: Snap Map is one of those settings that’s easy to forget after the initial setup. Before relying on Arrival Notifications, I take a quick look at who can still see my location to make sure I’m only sharing it with people I trust.

How to remove a saved place

Removing a place is straightforward. Press and hold the saved location under Arrival Notifications, then delete it.

    • I normally remove hotels and other temporary places once the trip is over. It keeps the saved list limited to the locations I actually use instead of filling it with places I’m unlikely to visit again.

    How to stop receiving Arrival Notifications from a friend

    You aren’t locked into receiving these alerts forever.

    1. Open your chat with the friend.
    2. Here, tap the blue linked location message.
    3. Now, tap Stop receiving this notification and confirm.

    The setting only affects Arrival Notifications. Your friendship, chat history, and other Snapchat features remain unchanged.

    When I wouldn’t recommend using Arrival Notifications

    Arrival Notifications only make sense if you’re already comfortable using Snap Map. Anyone who keeps Ghost Mode enabled most of the time or prefers not to give Snapchat continuous location access probably won’t get much value from the feature.

    I’d also leave it off if the people expecting your arrival updates don’t use Snapchat. In that case, sending a quick message through the app you already use is probably the more practical option.

    A small but useful feature…

    Arrival Notifications aren’t a headline feature, which is probably why many Snapchat users overlook them. For me, they’ve become one of those small conveniences that quietly remove a recurring task every time I travel.

    What’s your go-to way of letting someone know you’ve arrived safely? Tell us in the comments.

    In case you missed:

    • How to Mute Someone on Snapchat Without Blocking.
    • What do Snapchat symbols mean?
    • How to make emojis follow objects in Snapchat videos

title.rendered: How to unlock the Olivia Rodrigo Icon Series skins in Fortnite

content.rendered:
After strong rumors, Olivia Rodrigo finally arrived in Fortnite and joined its vast catalog of celebrity-based cosmetics. As a result, ardent fans of the American singer have been flocking to the online multiplayer title to bag the newly released items.

In 2026 itself, several Icon Series skins based on award-winning singers, such as Chappell Roan and Laufey, have been introduced in the game. With Rodrigo’s inclusion, Epic Games has incorporated another major name from the music industry to its ever-growing list of Fortnite collabs.

Like any special cosmetic, the Olivia Rodrigo skins in Fortnite are up for grabs for a limited time only, until July 25, 2026, at 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. If you want to add it to your inventory, just follow the steps below.

Steps to claim the Olivia Rodrigo skin in Fortnite

  1. Launch Fortnite and go to the cart icon tab (Shop tab).
  2. Next, scroll down to the Olivia Rodrigo promo and select the desired skin.
  3. Finally, hold the Purchase button to buy the item for 1,500 V-Bucks.

Other Olivia Rodrigo Fortnite cosmetics

1. Flammable Sticker Collection (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks

2. Olivia Butterfly Wings (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks

3. OR’s Guitar (pickaxe/back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

4. Olivia’s Mic (pickaxe/back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

5. Maggots for brains (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

6. Good 4 u (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

In addition to these, four different Olivia Rodrigo songs are available in the game as jam tracks. The titles included are Deja vu, Drop dead, Maggots for brains, and Vampire, each of which costs 500 V-Bucks.

Instead of purchasing individual cosmetics, you can purchase the Olivia Rodrigo Bundle priced at 3,200 V-Bucks, which consists of all the aforementioned outfits, back blings, pickaxes, emotes, and the “Maggots for brains” jam track. Doing so will save you a total of 2,900 V-Bucks, making it an attractive deal for those who want multiple items from this promotion.

More singer-themed Fortnite items coming soon

On July 29, a new Fortnite Festival season will begin and naturally bring with it a bunch of cosmetic items inspired by another popular musician. The ongoing season is being headlined by Laufey, but there is no solid word out about who may succeed her at the end of this month. Either way, music lovers can brace themselves for a fresh range of singer-inspired content coming to the Item Shop when the new season kicks off.

FAQs

How many Olivia Rodrigo skins are there in Fortnite?

There are two distinct Olivia Rodrigo skins currently available in Fortnite: SOUR Olivia Rodrigo and Lover Girl Olivia Rodrigo.

Which other singers have been added to Fortnite before?

Other singers and musicians previously added to Epic’s online game include Ariana Grande, Daft Punk, Sabrina Carpenter, Metallica, Billie Eilish, Bruno Mars, and more.

Which Olivia Rodrigo songs are available as Fortnite jam tracks right now?

Deja vu, Drop Dead, Maggots for brains, and Vampire can be bought and set as your Fortnite jam track.

In case you missed

  • How to get the Mongraal skin in Fortnite
  • How to get Gwenpool skin in Fortnite
  • How to get John Wick’s dog in Fortnite
  • How to get MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins in Fortnite

title.rendered: How to get the Mongraal skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Fortnite has expanded its Icon Series celebrity cosmetics with the addition of Mongraal, a popular Fortnite competitive gamer and streamer. However, it’s only available to claim for a limited time, so those interested should act right now.

For a brief time, on June 27, both Mongraal skins were available in the game as part of the Mongraal Icon Cup rewards. While that windows has closed, you can still grab these themed items in exchange for V-Bucks until July 7, 2026 by 10 PM PT or 1 PM ET.

Steps to claim Mongraal skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the cart icon tab (Shop tab).
  2. Scroll down to the Mongraal promo and select the Mongraal skin.
  3. Press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

Other Mongraal cosmetics in Fortnite

Apart from this one skin, there are several other in-game items inspired by Mongraal, from two unique pickaxes to a pair of flashy back blings, as listed below. These items sport elements and references deeply associated with the British gamer, such as his Epic Games display name “009” and his “Shing! Shing!” meme moment.

1. Elite Mongraal

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Bonus item: The Counter

2. The Counter (back bling)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

3. Lucky Clover (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

4. The Harvester (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks

5. Mongraalien (back bling)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

6. Shing Shing Shing (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

7. Clover Crush (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

Fortnite featuring famous internet personalities in its game is nothing new, and Mongraal’s arrival only confirms the developer still entrusts these collabs to bring more attention to the game. Given that he is someone who grew popular for winning Fortnite competitions, his addition to the Item Shop should be a move welcomed by ardent fans of the online game.

FAQs

Can I get Mongraal skin for free?

Not anymore. While it could have been obtained for free by achieving a high-enough rank in the Mongraal Icon Cup, that method no longer works as the online tournament has already expired.

How many Mongraal skins are there in Fortnite?

There are two. Apart from the vanilla version, there is also an alternate Mongraal skin that portrays him as sort of a masked agent.

Which other internet celebs are there in Fortnite?

Similar to Mongraal, other popular faces on the internet, including IShowSpeed, Ninja, and Loserfruit, have gone on to be featured as a Fortnite skin.

In case you missed

  • How to get Gwenpool skin in Fortnite
  • How to get galaxy sprites in Fortnite
  • How to get John Wick’s dog in Fortnite
  • How to restart Fortnite

title.rendered: Anime Destiny codes (July 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Anime Destiny codes on July 13, 2026

Anime Destiny is a Roblox tower defense game where summons and upgrades decide how long your team survives. Codes are useful early because free Gems, Shards, Cubes, and Malice give you more room to roll units and strengthen your roster before the grind gets annoying.

All working Anime Destiny codes

  • SBR!: 25 RR, 25 Cubes, 25 Malice, 1500 Gems (requires Level 15) (NEW)
  • 23rdPresident!: 25 RR and 1000 Gems (requires Level 5) (NEW)
  • Jojos!: 15 RR, 1000 Gems (requires Level 15) (NEW)
  • SorryForBugs!: Free Rewards (NEW)
  • JusticeForAD: 25 RR, 25 Cubes, 25 Malice, and 1000 Gems (NEW)
  • CursedAwakening: 15RR, 5 Capsules, and 500 Gems (NEW)
  • DomainExpansion: 10RR, 5000 Talismans, and 500 Gems (NEW)
  • ILoveAnimeDestiny!: 1,500 Gems, 15 Shards, 15 Cubes, and 15 Malice (NEW)
  • 3KCCU!: 2,000 Gems, 5,000 FrostLotus, 25 Shards, 35 Cubes, and 35 Malice
  • SorryForDelay: 500 Gems, 5 Cubes, 5 Shards, and 5 Malice
  • Release!: 1,500 Gems and 15 Shards

Start with these Anime Destiny codes before testing older strings. Copy them exactly, including the exclamation marks.

Expired Anime Destiny codes

These Anime Destiny codes are expired, older, or not safe to list as active anymore. Try them only after you finish the working list above.

ReleaseEA!, PATCHES!, PATCH!, BugPatch!, BugHOTFIX!, UPDATE 1, 6K Favorites, 6K Likes, FixedBugSrySrySry, Thx for 1M Visits!, Warped Ninja!!!, SryForShutdown, ShutdownIssue, ANIME DESTINY, 1K Favorites, Early Access!,

The active release code is Release!. If the all-caps RELEASE! fails, do not keep retrying it; use the exact working version from the list above.

How to redeem Anime Destiny codes

Anime Destiny keeps the code box on the right side of the screen, so you do not need to open a deep settings menu.

  1. Open Anime Destiny on Roblox.
  2. Click the Codes button on the right side of the screen.
  3. Paste a working code into the Enter Code box.
  4. Click Redeem to claim the reward.

If a new code fails on your first try, leave the game and join a fresh server before marking it expired.

If you want more free rewards, check out the latest Infection Gunfight codes, Mini War codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

Why an Anime Destiny code may not work

Most failed codes come down to one of these issues:

  • The code has expired after an update or shutdown fix.
  • You typed the wrong capitalization, missed an exclamation mark, or added an extra space.
  • You already redeemed the code on your Roblox account.
  • Your server has not refreshed after a new code drop.
  • The reward requires a new version of the game before it works everywhere.

For codes like ILoveAnimeDestiny! and 3KCCU!, copying and pasting is safer than typing manually.

Where to find more Anime Destiny codes

New Anime Destiny codes usually appear around launch events, concurrent-player milestones, update delays, and bug fixes. The best places to watch are the Anime Destiny Roblox page, the Anime Destiny Discord, and the Anime Destiny Trello.

You can also bookmark this page if you want the active list without digging through announcements.
